newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rubber stable in late trading.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rubber stable in late trading.

text.p: Indonesian tyre-grade SIR20 offer prices were generally stable in late trading on Monday amid thin buying interest and concerns that Thailand might sell its excess stocks, traders said.

"The market is likely to be more bearish tomorrow. There is a growing concern in the market that Thailand will sell its stocks. People have become more and more cautious," said one trader in Palembang, south Sumatra.
"We are still in the dark about the exact amount of the stocks. Some say it 70,000 tonnes, while others believe the stocks are around 140,000 tonnes," he said.
Traders said buyers were taking a wait-see-position also because movements in the rupiah.
"It's very bearish and sentiment is expected to stay the same tomorrow. Traders are offering rubber but no buyers are in sight," said one trader.
The rupiah was hovering around the 3,000 level against the dollar in thin late trading on Monday after briefly falling to 3,005, dealers said.
Rubber traders said SIR20 offer prices were quoted at 42.25 U.S. cents/lb fob Palembang for October shipment and at 42.50 for November shipment, but buyers were bidding at 40.00-41.50.
Offer prices were quoted at 42.00 fob Medan, they said.
